It increments the election term and requests votes from the other members. Each member votes for at most one candidate per term, and only if the candidate's oplog is at least as up to date as its own and the candidate has sufficient priority. A candidate that gets votes from a majority of voting members becomes the new primary. Because a majority is required, a network partition can't produce two primaries.
